product: U.S. Army woven tapestry throw blanket, olive drab with gold eagle seal, star border, fringed edge
niche: military blankets / veterans and military families

reasons: Niche identity: PASS. Veterans, military spouses and Army parents are one of the most defined tribes on the platform, and the seal names the tribe without a word of copy.
Novel format: FAIL. It is a woven throw. The object itself is not new to look at and the scroll does not stop for it on shape alone.
Giftability: PASS. Close to a pure gift item. Retirement, homecoming, Veterans Day, Father's Day.
Portable proof of concept: PASS. One unfold and the whole product is understood. No explaining, no voiceover needed.
Meme and share potential: FAIL. Nothing to send to a friend for its own sake. The only share is a tag on a relative who served, which is real but thin.
Where has this been my whole life: FAIL. It resolves no resentment. Nobody is annoyed by the absence of a blanket.
viral_dna.verdict: Weak on the filter. The two missing axes are novel format and problem-solving, and no prompt fixes that. It sells on emotion, not on demonstration, so the format has to carry what the object cannot.

photos.what: product photo, full flat lay of the blanket

reference.path_status: MISSING LOCALLY - reference lives only in Higgsfield storage; cloudfront is blocked by the egress proxy so it cannot be downloaded here. bin/cutsheet.sh and /edit both need a local file.

audio.how_it_reaches_the_final: bin/cutsheet.sh --build already muxes the reference track onto the finished video and drops every generated clip's own audio (-an per segment). Nothing needs adding for the soundtrack to be 1:1: it already is, for as long as the reference runs.
consequences: Clip 1's mouth movement is locked to 0.83-2.78s. Outside that window the lip sync visibly breaks.

The cup drop is a beat the original never had, so it has no sound of its own once the reference track is laid over. It is placed at 1.41s, the loudest transient in the reference, which is the only thing that covers it.
The second utterance at 4.80-5.92s falls over clip 2, which has nobody in frame. An off-screen voice there is fine and needs no lip sync.
Clips 3 and 4 run past the end of the reference, so they have no soundtrack under them at all.

plan.desc: Military surplus store aisle, handheld back camera. Man in his late 20s in OCP camo, short brown hair, light stubble, waist up. He is holding a clear plastic cup. Shock reaction, hand to mouth, the cup slips and drops to the floor, then he points off to the right. Camera whips right at the end of the beat, ending in motion blur so the join is invisible.
The pan lands on a retail shelf wall stacked with our own branded blanket boxes, four to six visible, identical. Slow handheld drift, no zoom. Tactical pouches and boots on the shelves around them.
plan.route_reason: IMG because the composition is the whole payoff and the packaging must be 1:1 with the locked box. T2V invents its own box art.

plan.desc: POV unboxing over a wooden table, soldier's sleeves and dog tags, box opened and blanket unfolded to the roundel. Student's own file.
The blanket on a wooden living-room floor, slow push in onto the eagle roundel. Student's own file.

notes: Trademark: U.S. Army marks and the Army seal are licensed through the Army Trademark Licensing Program. Selling merchandise carrying them without a licence is a live legal risk, separate from anything in this pipeline.
Format implication of the score: lead with the gifting or homecoming moment, not a product demo. The reveal is the unfold.
risks: The reference never shows the blanket. It sells a wall of packaging in a shop, which is retail credibility, not the emotional gift angle the 3/6 score pointed at. This format plays to the product's weakest side.

The payoff in the reference is a COMPETITOR brand (ARMYWORKS). /brand is mandatory before /prompts can write clip 2, and the box has to be designed from scratch: the uploaded photo is the blanket, not a box.
The reference has the actor holding a cup of beer inside a shop. Odd for this audience and a needless content-filter risk. Recommend dropping the prop.
The whip pan is the most motion-heavy second in the piece. Keep the motion sentence short in clip 1; overstuffed motion is the top cause of a bad generation.
Person appears only in clip 1, so no cross-clip identity lock is needed. That is the one thing this split makes easier.
Default cut detection finds ONE segment. Running /edit without --cuts 2.9 would map clip 1 onto the whole 6s and silently drop clip 2.

decisions.verdict: the cup is kept and dropped on the floor on the shock beat, not removed
ARMYWORKS confirmed as the student's own brand

brand.note: Student's own brand. The boxes in the reference are theirs, so this is not a competitor payoff after all.
